tasks.title: Derive wall PAINT area (perimeter x height) — the missing painting measurement
tasks.notes: A 2D plan has no wall height so painting gets ZERO auto-sqft today. Add wall height input + compute per-room paint area from perimeter × height.

prep.what: Add a wall-height input to the takeoff module so paint area (perimeter × height) can be computed per room and seeded as an estimate line.
prep.understand: The engine returns `meta.perimeter` per room in geometry, but `TakeoffEstimateSeeder` currently drops geometry on import. You need to preserve perimeter, add `wall_height_ft` to estimates, and compute wall paint SF = perimeter × height per room.
approach: Add migration: `estimates.wall_height_ft` (nullable float); wire into the takeoff seam input form and `TakeoffEstimateSeeder`.
In `TakeoffEstimateSeeder`, stop dropping geometry — preserve `meta.perimeter` per room from the engine response.
Compute `wall_paint_sqft = perimeter × wall_height_ft` per room; emit as a painting surface line via `LineItemFactory` using the painting `LaborRate` (seeded by t39).
Add a notice in Takeoff Review Vue: 'Wall height missing — paint area will be zero' when height is not set on the estimate.
resources: Engine room geometry: meta.perimeter field in measurement response

tasks.title: Route takeoff measurements to trades at the seam
tasks.notes: Every measurement collapses into one anonymous kind=custom $0 line, dropping kind+geometry. Preserve+switch on kind: area(SF)->flooring, wall SF->painting, line(LF)->trim, count(EA)->doors/tile.

prep.what: Fix `TakeoffEstimateSeeder` to route each measurement by kind to the right trade instead of collapsing everything to a generic $0 custom line.
prep.understand: The seeder loses kind+geometry on import. The fix is a switch on `measurement->kind` that maps to the right `LineItemFactory` method and uses the core-vs-subbed helper (`ProjectType::isCoreTrade()`) to assign `crew_type`.
approach: In `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` add a switch on `$measurement->kind`: 'area' → flooring, 'wall_paint' → painting, 'line' → trim/wall-linear, 'count' → doors/tile.
Use `ProjectType::isCoreTrade()` + `ProjectType::group()` to assign `crew_type` (own_team vs subcontractor) per trade.
Map each kind to its unit (sqft, lf, ea) and appropriate `rate_type` via `LineItemFactory`.
Write a test: seed a takeoff with all 4 measurement kinds, assert correct kind/trade/crew_type on each resulting estimate line.

tasks.title: Add PerLinearFt RateType (prerequisite for pricing trim/wall-linear)
tasks.notes: RateType has no per-linear-foot. Small enum+factory+seeder change. Unblocks t48 (pricing trim lines).

prep.what: Add `per_linear_ft` to the RateType enum, wire its unit label through LineItemFactory, and seed a trim LaborRate with it.
prep.understand: This is a pure PHP enum + factory + seeder change — no DB migration needed. `LineItemFactory::unitFromRateType()` maps rate types to unit labels ('lf'). After this lands, t48 (price trim lines by LF) is unblocked.
approach: Add `PerLinearFt = 'per_linear_ft'` to `app/Enums/RateType.php` with label 'Per Linear Foot'.
Update `LineItemFactory::unitFromRateType()` to return `'lf'` for `PerLinearFt`.
Add a trim LaborRate row in `LaborRateSeeder.php` using `PerLinearFt` rate_type.
Quick unit test: seed a trim LaborRate, assert `unit = 'lf'` on the factory output.

tasks.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text firms + callout-vs-room filtering
tasks.notes: Rooms show 'unnamed' on outlined-text PDFs. M3 tiles spike exists (~4.3 min/sheet). Productize as opt-in 'read labels (AI)' + filter callout noise.

prep.what: Build an AI-powered room-label reading lane using MiniMax M3 vision for PDFs that outline all text, plus filter non-room callouts (UP arrows, FEC boxes, general-note paragraphs) from label matches.
prep.understand: The free text lane returns zero room names when the PDF outlines text. The M3 tiles spike in `docs/spike/run_labels_m3tiles.py` costs ~$0.005/sheet (metered, PRD §7a) and is too expensive to run on every upload — it must be opt-in. Callout filtering is a separate problem: holabird shows noise like 'UP', 'FEC', stair arrows matching as room names. MINIMAX_AI key must reach the VPS before this can go to prod (a secrets decision coordinated with the t13 pattern).
approach: Review `docs/spike/run_labels_m3tiles.py` and `engine/labels.py` to understand the current label pipeline and where the M3 hook will live.
Productize: add a `use_ai_labels` flag (default False) + PRD §7a metered-credits event so it only fires when the user explicitly triggers 'read labels (AI)'.
Add callout-vs-room filtering in the label post-processor: reject single-token directional/code callouts (UP/DOWN/FEC), paragraph-length strings, known non-room prefix patterns.
Add a TODO comment noting the MINIMAX_AI key VPS secrets step required before enabling this in prod.

tasks.title: Assemblies-per-room → paint/drywall/flooring quantities + wall heights
tasks.notes: assemblies-lite scaffolded in engine/assemblies.py (B1). Full version = classification → assembly formulas → up to 8 quantities. Last pillar before estimator-grade Excel.

prep.what: Expand `engine/assemblies.py` from a scaffold into a full formula-driven assembly library: classification → up to 8 derived quantity lines (paint walls, paint ceiling, drywall, floor, etc.) with default wall-height handling.
prep.understand: assemblies-lite is already wired into `build_sheet_takeoff` and the Excel lane. The full version drives a `classification → AssemblyTemplate` mapping with parameterized formulas: paint_walls = perimeter × height, floor = area, drywall = 2 × perimeter × height. CSI trade codes apply (div 09 for finishes). Wall heights default to a global configurable when not stored per-room.
approach: Audit `engine/assemblies.py` scaffolding: understand the current AssemblyLine/AssemblyQuantity data model and what's already wired.
Define an `ASSEMBLY_LIBRARY` dict: `classification → list[AssemblyLine(kind, formula_fn, unit, csi_code)]`. Start with the 4 core: paint_walls, paint_ceiling, floor, drywall.
Implement formula functions using `Room.area`, `Room.perimeter`, and `wall_height_ft` (from Room metadata or a global default parameter). Return `AssemblyQuantity` objects.
Wire assembly quantities into `build_sheet_takeoff` orchestrator and the Excel export — either as an Assemblies tab or as expanded takeoff rows per room.
